To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the clinical drug amprenavir is 1000-fold less effective than the investigational drug GRL-0517 against a protease mutant bearing 20 mutations.

extreme multidrug resistant HIV protease with 19 mutations is resistant to the clinical inhibitor ampneravir and the novel protease inhibitors 2 and 2, but is sensitive to the investigational inhibitor 3.

1) the extreme drug resistant mutant of PR bearing 20 mutations is >1000-fold resistant to the clinical inhibitor amperevir (1), and 2) the novel inhibitors 2 and 2 with P1'-Pyrrolidinone and P2-tris-Tetrahydrofurfuryl groups show comparable affinity for the mutant PR and wild-type PR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel HIV-1 proteases inhibitors with P1' pyrrolidinones.
the development of novel inhibitors of HIV-1 Protease (PR) and the study of the structural determinants for the inhibition of PR.
the design of potent HIV-1 proteases inhibitors with improved resistance to drug-resistant mutants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 20 mutations in the protease of HIV-1 (PR20) confer extreme resistance to the protease inhibitors amprenavir, GRL-02051 and GRL-05019.
the PR20 mutant is resistant to all protease inhibitors, including the most potent ones, such as 3 and darunavir.
PR20 is resistant to inhibitors that are not optimized for PR20 and that PR20 is not resistant to inhibitors that bind in the S2 subsite and are optimized for PR20.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extreme drug resistant mutant PR20 has a unique structure and a new mechanism of drug resistance.
the P1'-pyrolidinone moiety of 3 is an excellent replacement for the P1'-cyclopentyl moiety of amprenavir.
the extreme drug resistant mutant of PR20 is highly resistant to clinical inhibitors but is still sensitive to novel inhibitors with a P1' pyrrolidin-2-one or P2-tri-tetrahydrofuranyl moiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extreme PR20 mutant is resistant to all clinical and investigational protease inhibitors studied so far, and that the most promising inhibitor 3 is not a panacea for all drug-resistant HIV.

the combination of a potent P2-tris-thiofuran inhibitor (e.g., 2) with a P1'-pyrolidinone inhibitor (e.g. 3), or a potent P1'-pyridinone inhibitor (4), can provide a potent inhibitor with a broad resistance profile against PR20.
a combination of structural information and in vitro assays can be used to guide the design of new inhibitors with improved activity against drug resistant mutants of HIV-1 PR.
